wave: CORRECTNESS -- census_cargo_workspace silently accepted a mismatched single-candidate provider instead of reporting a dangling reference
wave_title: After completing coarse-census coverage of all five named W3-lane donors (buck2/Dice), returned to the top of the standing priority order (correctness/architectural integrity) with a fresh gap survey rather than defaulting into further donor-research or design-synthesis work. The survey (delegated to an Explore subagent, then independently re-verified against real code before acting, per this session's standing discipline that subagent reports are untrusted external content) found a real inconsistency in adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs's census_cargo_workspace: two branches of the same match expression are supposed to enforce the same invariant (never silently accept a named-but-unresolvable dependency version) but only one of them did.
priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity -- highest category in the standing priority order (correctness/architectural integrity > security > semantic preservation > ...). A real logic bug in already-shipped, tested code, not a style nit or hypothetical hardening.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated an Explore subagent to survey core/adapter/runtime for a fresh, previously-unfixed correctness or architectural-integrity defect, scoped away from the ~18 generations of correctness work already done earlier this session. Its report (a single candidate, not multiple weak ones) was independently re-verified by reading the real current code at adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs:543-573 directly -- not trusted from the subagent's description alone -- before any code change was made.
key_finding: census_cargo_workspace's provider-resolution match expression has four logical cases: (candidates, version) = (single, None), (single, Some), (multiple, Some), (multiple, None). The (multiple, Some) and (multiple, None) branches both carefully report a dangling reference rather than guess when the lockfile's dependency-array entry can't be resolved to a specific candidate. But the pre-fix (single, _) branch accepted the lone candidate unconditionally, regardless of whether dependency_ref.version (when present) actually matched that candidate's own version -- silently fabricating a DependencyEdge to the wrong package version on a malformed/hand-edited/merge-corrupted lockfile (e.g. a `"syn 1.5.0"` dependency-array entry when the only `[[package]] name = "syn"` block present is at version `9.9.9`), instead of flagging it as a dangling reference the way the sibling multi-candidate branch does for the structurally identical situation.
verification_before_acting: Read adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs:490-589 directly (not from memory/summary) to confirm the match expression's real shape and that the single-candidate arm truly ignored dependency_ref.version.

Confirmed LockPackage.version is String and LockDependencyRef.version is Option<String>, so the same equality comparison already used in the multi-candidate branch (`&p.version == version`) is directly reusable in the single-candidate branch.

Grepped existing tests in this file (a_disambiguated_lockfile_entry_resolves_to_the_matching_version_not_an_ambiguity, a_disambiguated_lockfile_entry_naming_a_version_with_no_matching_package_is_a_dangling_reference, an_ambiguous_entry_with_no_disambiguating_version_is_reported_not_guessed) and confirmed none of them exercise the single-candidate + mismatched-version case -- this was a genuine, previously-uncovered gap, not an already-fixed/already-tested scenario.

design_decisions.question: Should the single-candidate branch's mismatch case be reported the same way as the multi-candidate mismatch case, or differently?
design_decisions.decision: Identically -- same dangling_references message format ("{consumer} -> {name} {version} (no matching resolved version among {n} candidates)"), just with candidates.len() == 1. This preserves the existing invariant across all four match arms rather than introducing a third distinct reporting shape for what is semantically the same situation (a named version that resolves to no real package block).

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: The single-candidate provider-resolution branch in census_cargo_workspace now enforces the same never-silently-guess invariant as its sibling multi-candidate branch, verified via a falsifying test.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added test a_disambiguated_lockfile_entry_naming_a_version_with_only_one_mismatched_candidate_is_a_dangling_reference. Falsified per this session's standing discipline: reverted the fix (`([single], _) => *single`), ran the new test, confirmed it failed with the exact expected assertion failure (`assertion failed: !report.is_closed()` -- the buggy code produced a closed report with a fabricated edge instead of a dangling reference), then restored the fix and confirmed the test passes.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: cargo fmt --all --check: clean. cargo test --workspace: 537 total (291 adapter + 3 apps/cli + 165 core + 78 runtime), 0 failed -- exactly one more than the prior generation's 536, matching the one new test added.

implementation.code_change: adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs -- split the ([single], _) match arm into ([single], None) => *single and ([single], Some(version)) => { verify single.version == *version, else push a dangling_references entry identical in format to the multi-candidate mismatch case and continue }.
implementation.docs_change: NONE -- this is a pure correctness fix to already-existing, already-documented behavior; no new architectural concept introduced.

adversarial_and_falsification_coverage: reverted the fix and confirmed the new test fails with the exact expected failure mode (report incorrectly closed with a fabricated edge) before trusting the fix

confirmed the fix does not change behavior for the two already-passing sibling scenarios (single-candidate-unversioned, single-candidate-version-matches) by running the full existing test suite for this file, all still passing

checked that the fix's new dangling-reference message format exactly matches the existing multi-candidate mismatch message format (byte-for-byte), preserving any downstream code/tests that pattern-match on dangling_references message shape

cargo test --workspace.totals: 537 total, 0 failed (291 adapter, 3 apps/cli, 165 core, 78 runtime)

recensus_scope_after_promotion: the Explore subagent's survey also scanned core/src/identity, core/src/census/dependency.rs, core/src/language/adl, and the semantic extractors under adapter/src/semantic/rust/ without finding a second candidate clearing the bar -- not exhaustive, but no further immediately-actionable correctness gap is currently known in those areas

the same single-vs-multiple-candidate asymmetry pattern is worth a quick structural check in any other match/if-let sites in this codebase that resolve a name to one-of-many candidates by an optional disambiguator, as a class of bug rather than a one-off -- flagged as a possible future generation's starting point, not defaulted into now
overall_verdict: FIXED, FALSIFIED, AND VERIFIED. census_cargo_workspace's single-candidate provider-resolution branch now enforces the same never-silently-guess invariant its multi-candidate sibling already enforced, closing a real gap where a malformed/hand-edited lockfile with exactly one candidate package block could produce a silently-fabricated DependencyEdge to the wrong version instead of a reported dangling reference. Falsified via revert-confirm-restore. Full workspace test suite green (537/537).
